text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we still have open questions about how tenant burst behavior should interact with priority and quota reconciliation. Wanted to put the proposed change in a thread and get quick alignment.

chetan: TL;DR of the proposal?

maria: Proposal sketch — introduce a small, time-windowed priority credit pool per tenant that: 1) is charged against tenant quota only when used beyond baseline reservations, 2) decays over a sliding window (so short bursts cost less than sustained bursts), and 3) can be preempted based on global priority bands.

oliver: Sounds promising. Two immediate questions: how do we prevent starvation for low-priority tenants during cluster-wide surges, and how do we observe/alert on misuse?

maria: For starvation we propose a soft floor: every tenant keeps a guaranteed minimal token runway (configurable by SLA tier). If global pressure is high we proportionally throttle rather than zero them out. For observability we emit these metrics: `tenant.burst_tokens.used`, `tenant.burst_tokens.decay_rate`, `tenant.burst_throttle_events`.

anya: Do we have a simple admission circuit we can implement in the operator so it's rollback-safe? We should avoid touching allocator core until we're comfortable.

jade: Agree with canary-safety. My suggestion: implement admission as a shim controller that sits between API intent and the operator. It rewrites admission verdicts with an extra `burst_allowance` field; the operator ignores it if flag=false. Rollout path: shim off -> shim on (opt-in tenants) -> default on.

oliver: Nice. Can you sketch the config?

maria: Example config snippet: ```yaml
burstPolicy:
  window_seconds: 60
  bucket_size: 5        # number of burst tokens
  baseline_charge: true # only charge over reserved baseline
  decay_alpha: 0.2      # exponential decay factor per window
  preemptible_priority_band: low
  soft_floor_percent: 0.01 # 1% guaranteed capacity at high contention
```

chetan: Implementation notes: the admission shim needs to consult two signals: current pool headroom (from operator telemetry) and tenant token balance (from quota service). We should avoid synchronous calls per request — use a small local cache + watch stream so admission is often local.

anya: On the metrics side, add `burst_token_replenish` and tag by rollout stage (canary|default). Alerts: spike in `burst_throttle_events` or sustained `burst_tokens.used` > 80% for >5m should page eng-runtime.

jade: One more tradeoff: do we bill burst use immediately or at end of window? Immediate billing is simpler but harsh for noisy neighbors; end-of-window amortized billing is friendlier but harder for accounting/chargebacks. Thoughts?

maria: Leaning to amortized billing at the end of the window with a hard cap that prevents abuse mid-window. That way UX is smoother and we can show a daily reconciliation. We'll need an idempotent reconciliation job.

chetan: For preemption semantics: when global capacity low, preempt tenants by lowest effective SLA score = (tier_weight * reserved_share) + recent_sla_violations. We should avoid oscillations — add a cooldown per tenant (default 2m) after preemption.

oliver: Ops concerns: ensure operator can evict without corrupting in-flight KV caches. Eviction should drain gracefully and expose a `eviction_intent` trace that runtime can surface.

maria: Good call. Add `eviction_intent` event in trace and tie it to `fallback_model_variant` policy so we avoid hard failures.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary admission-shim v0.1 has been scheduled for cluster `staging-gpu-01` (eta 02:15 UTC).

anya: Rollout plan: 1) implement shim + metrics + reconciliation job in a feature branch, 2) run internal canary with low-traffic tenants, 3) monitor `burst_throttle_events`, `p99_latency`, cost delta for 24h, 4) enable opt-in for more tenants, 5) default on with billing reconciliation.

jade: Danger notes: watch for tricky interactions with existing warmup heuristics — bursts can trigger mass prewarms that defeat cost goals. We should add a guard: if burst_token_used triggers prewarm more than X times in window, temporarily disable auto-prewarm for that tenant.

maria: Next concrete tasks: @chetan to prototype the shim + local cache (owner), @oliver to add telemetry hooks in operator (owner), @anya to draft alert runbook (owner). I'll wire product config and billing reconciliation spec.

chetan: I'll put up a draft PR for the shim by EOD tomorrow.

oliver: I'll PR the telemetry changes and expose the new metrics as Prometheus labels.

anya: I'll start a brief runbook and add the initial alerts to PagerDuty staging.

maria: Great — thanks all. We'll sync in the weekly runtime sync; if anyone hits a blocker ping here. :thumbsup:
